Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are David Harrington, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Ellis, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Harrington.

David Harrington:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on four key aspects: capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, overview of key financial performance highlights, impact of seasonality or external factors such as the flu season, and impact of recent acquisitions on financial performance.

Let me begin with our capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, which remain a cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in the dynamic healthcare services and hospitals sector. In the third quarter, we deployed $285 million in CapEx, bringing our year-to-date spend to $825 million, tracking squarely toward our full-year guidance of $1.15 to $1.25 billion. This equates to about 5.8% of our trailing twelve-month revenue of $22.4 billion, aligning with the industry median for acute care operators like HCA Healthcare and Universal Health Services, who are guiding 5-7% of revenue this year amid similar inflationary pressures on construction and equipment costs.

Breaking it down, roughly 62% of our Q3 CapEx, or $177 million, supported facility modernization initiatives across our 48-hospital footprint, while the remaining 38%, or $108 million, fueled expansion projects. Year-over-year, total CapEx rose 18%, reflecting a deliberate acceleration following our 2023 deleveraging phase. This compares favorably to Community Health Systems' more conservative 10-12% CapEx-to-revenue ratio, underscoring our stronger balance sheet with net debt-to-EBITDAR at 3.2x versus their 5.5x.

On the modernization front, we're intensely focused on boosting operational efficiency, patient safety, and clinical outcomes to align with value-based care reimbursement models under Medicare Advantage, which now makes up 42% of our payer mix, up from 35% two years ago. Key efforts included $45 million for digital transformation, upgrading our enterprise-wide Epic MyChart EHR platform to the latest Willow Ambulatory and Beaker modules. This rollout is now 85% complete across our Southeast and Midwest markets, already cutting length-of-stay by 0.4 days on average in pilot hospitals, lifting case mix index by 2.5% and supporting our 3% same-facility revenue growth.

We also allocated $62 million to advanced diagnostics and OR technology, such as installing three new 3T Siemens Magnetom MRI systems and two GE Optima CT scanners with AI-enabled dose reduction. At our flagship Orlando campus, we're adding five more Intuitive Surgical da Vinci Xi robotic systems, aiming for a 15% rise in minimally invasive procedures that deliver 20-25% higher margins than open surgeries.

Additionally, $35 million went toward sustainability and resilience upgrades, including Trane HVAC systems with IoT predictive maintenance and solar microgrids at five Sunbelt facilities. These position us for LEED Silver certification on 70% of our portfolio by 2026, meeting ESG mandates from investors like BlackRock and Vanguard, while trimming utility costs by 12-15% amid 8% year-over-year energy inflation in hospital operations.

Regionally, modernization spending was heaviest in the Southeast at 45% of the total, driven by Florida's aging boomer population projected to add 1.2 million Medicare lives by 2030 according to CMS data, necessitating cutting-edge stroke and cardiology centers. Meanwhile, our Midwest rural hospitals received $22 million for tele-ICU expansions through Teladoc integrations, tackling nurse staffing shortages with vacancy rates lingering at 18% per NSI Nursing Solutions data.

Shifting to expansion, our $108 million Q3 investment reflects a disciplined de novo approach amid 4-5% national inpatient utilization growth, propelled by pent-up elective volumes and GLP-1 drug-driven bariatric demand. Highlights encompass opening 120 licensed acute beds across three projects, including a 72-bed tower at our Phoenix ASC network, plus six new outpatient surgery centers totaling 24 ORs. These OSCs, modeled on HCA's freestanding approach, target 30% EBITDA margins at maturity with payback in 24-36 months through reduced overhead and site-neutral reimbursements.

We advanced $40 million on two 8-bed micro-hospitals in high-growth Texas suburbs in the Dallas-Fort Worth MSA, partnering with USPI for ortho and GI focus. This echoes Tenet Healthcare's playbook, aiming to capture 15-20% market share in underserved areas with average daily census ramping to 5.5 beds in year one.

These investments fit our hub-and-spoke model: modernizing hub tertiary centers for high-acuity cases while expanding spokes for high-margin outpatient shifts, where volumes grew 22% year-over-year per Definitive Healthcare data. We're countering 6% national construction cost overruns per Mortenson Construction data with fixed-price EPC contracts and steel hedging. Our ROI models forecast 14-16% IRR on this portfolio, generating incremental EBITDA of $180 million by fiscal 2027, with 60% funded organically.

Moving ahead, we anticipate Q4 CapEx at $300-320 million, leaning toward expansion as we break ground on a 200-bed replacement hospital in Atlanta's northern suburbs. This sets us up to exceed peers in adjusted admissions growth, guiding at 4.5%, even as we manage reimbursement pressures like the 2.9% IPPS cut.

Next, let's turn to an overview of our key financial performance highlights. As a leading operator of 185 acute care hospitals and over 1,200 outpatient facilities across 28 states, we're thrilled with another quarter of strong results in this evolving healthcare environment. These outcomes highlight the strength of our diversified platform, tight cost discipline, and targeted investments in growth areas like ambulatory services and digital health.

On the top line, total net revenues hit $4.72 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year and 6.1% on a same-facility basis, excluding our recent tuck-in acquisition of three hospitals in the Dallas-Fort Worth area from a regional nonprofit. This extends our streak to 11 straight quarters of same-facility revenue growth. Key drivers included 4.3% same-facility admissions growth—our best in two years—spurred by pent-up demand for elective orthopedics and cardiology, plus a 2.8% rise in average daily census to 28,400 beds. Patient days climbed 5.1% to 2.61 million, with revenue per patient day up 3.4% to $1,812, aided by a 1.9% increase in case mix index to 1.82 amid higher post-COVID acuity.

Net patient service revenues, 92% of our total, surged 8.7% to $4.35 billion. Commercial managed care rates rose 5.2% on renewals, surpassing Medicare's 2.8% IPPS adjustment and flat Medicaid amid redeterminations. Payer mix stayed stable: 48% commercial, 32% Medicare, 15% Medicaid, 5% self-pay/other. Our value-based care contracts, now 22% of commercial lives versus 18% last year, generated $145 million in shared savings, up 25%, via ties with UnitedHealthcare and Humana's CenterWell.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $785 million, up 12.4% year-over-year, with margins expanding to 16.6% from 15.2%—our strongest Q3 since 2019. Same-facility EBITDA grew 10.9%, driven by revenue leverage and cost controls. Diluted adjusted EPS climbed 18% to $1.42, topping expectations thanks to reduced interest from Q1 refinancing and a 15% share reduction via our $2 billion buyback.

Volumes showed solid trends: inpatient admissions at 512,000, up 4.3% same-facility, with surgical volumes—our top-margin area—jumping 7.1% on 12% growth in joint replacements and spinal fusions. Outpatient revenues soared 14.5% to $1.28 billion, or 27% of total versus 24% prior year. Our 450+ ASCs and imaging centers posted 22% same-facility growth, riding the site-of-service shift. ED visits rose 3.2% to 2.15 million, observation stays up 6% on acuity.

Costs shone through, with operating expenses dropping 110 basis points to 83.4% of revenue. Labor, 48% of revenues, grew just 5.8% despite 4.2% RN wage inflation and shortages—our VitaFlex model mixing agency, travel nurses, and ShiftMed tech cut agency spend 28% sequentially. Supplies rose 6.9% but held at 2.1% of revenues via HealthTrust GPO savings of $62 million on implants and drugs. Pharmacy costs stabilized post-Inflation Reduction Act.

By region, Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, Carolinas, 62% of EBITDA—saw 9.5% same-facility revenue growth from migration and Medicaid dynamics. Texas gained from EPIC EHR go-lives at five sites, improving charge capture 4% and denials below 2%. Northeast/Midwest faced redetermination drags trimming admissions 1.2%, offset by 6% commercial growth in urban anchors like Chicago and Philadelphia.

These results reinforce our growth-plus-efficiency strategy. Year-to-date CapEx hit $450 million, with $120 million for 45 da Vinci systems and $85 million for telehealth supporting 35% of outpatient visits, slashing no-shows 40%. Our de novo ASC pipeline has 15 sites for Q4 starts at 20% margins. M&A integration in DFW is on pace for 250 bps 2025 accretion. With $1.2 billion liquidity and 3.1x leverage, we're set to outperform amid inflation and reimbursement risks.

We're raising full-year 2024 guidance: revenues $18.9-$19.1 billion, adjusted EBITDA $3.15-$3.22 billion, diluted adjusted EPS $5.65-$5.80.

Now, regarding the impact of seasonality or external factors, like this year's severe flu season that began building momentum in late Q3, our performance highlighted how respiratory illnesses can create both tailwinds and strains in our cyclically sensitive industry, akin to peers HCA Healthcare and Universal Health Services. Consolidated net patient revenues reached $2.85 billion for the quarter, up 14% year-over-year and 12% same-facility. This stemmed from an 18% inpatient admissions surge to 145,000 across our 52 hospitals and 120 ASCs. Flu-related cases made up 22% of admissions—highest in five years versus 11% prior—driven by a virulent H3N2 strain, 45% more severe per CDC than 2022-23, spiking ED volumes 25% to 1.2 million and ADC to 18,500 beds, up 16%.

Service lines felt distinct effects: respiratory admissions for pneumonia, flu, COPD up 28%, lifting CMI 3.2% to 1.85 and revenue per admission 9% to $21,400, shifting payer mix toward commercial at 145% of Medicare. ALOS stretched to 4.7 days from 4.3 on ventilated cases. Northeast hospitals saw 32% flu spikes worsened by cold weather, cutting electives 8% and contracting EBITDA margins 220 bps to 18.5% with $45 million extra staffing. Sunbelt Texas/Florida facilities had 14% admissions growth but margin expansion of 150 bps to 24.2% via 12% faster ED throughput with AI triage.

Other factors included 5,000 extra pediatric RSV cases and 8% COVID contributions. We handled CMS's 2.9% IPPS and 3.7% OPPS updates, offset by 1.5% Medicaid mix hit from redeterminations. Expenses rose 17% to $2.42 billion: supplies up 11% on IV/PPE shortages, labor up 22% at 52% of revenues with 19% nurse turnover. EBITDA margins dipped 180 bps to 21.4%, but adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $612 million; net income $185 million or $1.42 diluted EPS, beating by $0.08.

Proactively, our FluShield Initiative with $75 million in predictive analytics via Epic and Google Cloud AI forecasted peaks at 92% accuracy, enabling pre-staffing and stockpiling. Virtual nursing hubs now handle 25% monitoring; Amwell tele-ED grew 40% QoQ, taking 12% flu visits virtually at $150 reimbursements. For FY25, we see moderated flu at +8-10% Q1 admissions, guiding 5-7% same-facility revenue and 23% EBITDA margins via 15% agency cuts and Vizient GPO savings.

Finally, the impact of recent acquisitions has been a major driver. We're spotlighting our January 2024 $850 million purchase of Southeast Surgical Partners, a top ASC platform with 12 facilities in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas, and our July tuck-in of Tri-State Community Hospitals, a three-hospital system in Knoxville, Tennessee, with 450 beds and strong Medicare Advantage links.

These added $215 million in Q3 revenue, 14% of our $1.52 billion total, up 12% year-over-year. Pro forma full SSP quarter, growth hits 18% versus 7% same-facility on 4% case volume and 2% CMI to 1.68 in high-acuity ortho/cardio. EBITDA from assets: $52 million at 24% margins, 400 bps above legacy 20%, lifting company EBITDA margin 150 bps to 21.8% and total to $332 million, up 16%. Ex-integration costs of $12 million for EMR/supply, accretive $0.18 to EPS, fueling 22% growth.

Synergies beat targets: $18 million run-rate, 25% ahead of $25 million Year 1, with 60% from Vizient GPO 12-15% savings on implants/pharma, 40% from revenue cycle centralization cutting AR days to 42. Cross-referrals up 22% for joints/GI to ASCs, aligning with site-neutral CMS 2025 OPPS. Payer mix improved to 42% commercial. Sunbelt bed share now 65% from 52%; SSP in growth MSAs with 52% MA, Knoxville density for bundles at 2.1 ALOS/85% occupancy.

These tap outpatient/value-based trends: 70% SSP volume under Humana/United narrow networks post-expansion; Meditech AI optimizes ORs for 10% utilization gain, 15% no-show drop. FY25: 10-12% organic growth, $40 million synergies, 8-10% EPS accretion post $15 million capex. SSP payback 2.2x in 24 months at 8.5x EBITDA multiple.

These deals transform us, countering 4.2% labor inflation, targeting 12-15% EBITDA CAGR.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Rachel to review our financial results in more detail.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David outlined, we delivered a solid quarter. Net revenue for Q3 was $4.72 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth stemmed from higher patient volumes, favorable case mix, and outpatient momentum.

Our operating expenses were $3.93 billion, representing 83.4% of net revenue. We're steadfast in cost management while investing in growth like digital tools and ambulatory expansion.

Adjusted net income for the quarter was $265 million, or $1.42 per diluted share. We're pleased with this performance and confident in hitting our elevated full-year targets.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to David.

David Harrington:
Thank you, Rachel. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of the flu season and other external factors on your operations?

David Harrington:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, the flu season's early buildup in late Q3 was notable, with H3N2 driving 22% of admissions across our network, up sharply from prior year. ED volumes spiked 25%, pushing ADC higher, which benefited revenues through elevated acuity and CMI gains. Regionally, it challenged our Northeast sites with staffing premiums, but Sunbelt efficiency held margins firm. Our predictive tools and telehealth mitigated diversions effectively, turning potential strain into volume upside while planning for normalization ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?

Rachel Kim:
Thanks, Mike. We're guiding for 4-5% same-facility admissions growth in Q4, building on Q3's 4.3% with continued elective recovery and outpatient shift. Flu moderation should ease acuity pressures, but we're factoring 8-10% respiratory lift early on. Acquisitions add tailwinds, and CapEx ramps support capacity. Overall, same-facility revenue 5-7%, with EBITDA margins recovering toward 23% on efficiencies.

Operator:
Our next question is from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. On the acquisitions, how are synergies tracking and any update on ROI?

Rachel Kim:
Hi Lisa. Synergies are ahead at $18 million run-rate, exceeding targets via GPO and revenue cycle wins. Cross-referrals are strong at 22% uplift, enhancing margins. We're on track for $40 million full-year, 8-10% EPS accretion, with payback multiples under 2.5x as modeled, positioning us well in Sunbelt growth pockets.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to David Harrington for closing remarks.

David Harrington:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
